bib.title: Semantic Parsing on Freebase from Question-Answer Pairs
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2013 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 1533-1544

question: Can a semantic parser that scales to Freebase's thousands of predicates be trained from question-answer pairs alone, without annotated logical forms?
hypothesis: Coarse alignment of text to the KB plus a bridging operation that generates predicates from neighbouring predicates narrows the predicate space enough to learn from denotations.
contributions: A coarse phrase-to-predicate lexicon built by aligning ReVerb/ClueWeb09 triples to Freebase
A bridging operation generating binary predicates from neighbouring unaries or event variables
Log-linear model with POS, rule-count and denotation-size features that soft-encode composition rules
WEBQUESTIONS, a new question-answer dataset from Google Suggest and Amazon Mechanical Turk, plus SEMPRE code release

method.summary: A beam-based bottom-up semantic parser (SEMPRE) builds derivations over lambda-DCS logical forms using an alignment lexicon and bridging, scored by a log-linear model trained to maximise the log-likelihood of derivations whose denotation equals the gold answer. Evaluated on FREE917 (Cai and Yates 2013) and the new WEBQUESTIONS.
method.task: semantic parsing / question answering over Freebase from question-answer pairs

datasets.name: Freebase (2013-06-09 dump)
datasets.source: Google 2013 data dump; copy queried with Virtuoso via SPARQL
datasets.preprocessing: Properties from domains user and base filtered for alignment

datasets.name: Aligned ReVerb triples from ClueWeb09
datasets.size: 15M triples; 55,081 typed binary phrases (9,456 untyped), 6,299 unary phrases; lexicon graph 109K binary edges, 294K unary edges
datasets.source: Lin et al. 2012 subset with subject entities linked to KB; objects linked by string matching
datasets.preprocessing: Lemmatised, typed with Freebase types, dates normalised with SUTime

datasets.name: FREE917
datasets.split: 30% held out for test; remaining 70% for development, of which 512 train / 129 validation (80/20), dev numbers averaged over 3 random splits
datasets.preprocessing: Logical forms converted to simple lambda-DCS and executed to get answers; manual 1,100-entry entity lexicon used

datasets.name: WEBQUESTIONS
datasets.size: 5,810 examples; 4,525 word types (from 1M questions visited, 100K sent to AMT, 6,642 annotated identically by at least two workers)
datasets.split: 35% random subset held out for test; remaining 65% divided 80/20 into train and validation
datasets.source: Google Suggest breadth-first search from 'Where was Barack Obama born?'; answers from Amazon Mechanical Turk at $0.03 per question; released at nlp.stanford.edu/software/sempre/
datasets.preprocessing: Entities mapped with a Lucene index over 41M Freebase entities; wh-word questions with exactly one entity; each query yields 5 candidate questions

models.name: SEMPRE parser (alignment + bridging)
models.architecture: log-linear model over derivations, beam-based bottom-up parser, simple lambda-DCS

other.hand_written_rules: 17 rules mapping question words to logical forms

models.name: Cai and Yates (2013)
models.architecture: CCG semantic parser trained on full logical forms

models.name: Ablated baseline (no bridging, no denotation features, no alignment features)

training.objective: maximise log-likelihood of derivations with correct denotation, summed over latent derivations: O(theta)=sum_i log sum_{d: [[d.z]]=y_i} p(d|x_i), approximated on the beam
training.optimizer: AdaGrad (stochastic gradient ascent, per-feature step size)
training.compute: about 600,000 SPARQL queries for a full run over WEBQUESTIONS training examples
training.seeds: dev numbers averaged over 3 random splits; no seed values

other.lexicalized_features: added on WEBQUESTIONS test run, omitted on FREE917 test run (overfitting)

inference.decoding: answer predicted from the derivation with highest probability on the beam
inference.samples: single prediction per question; dev averaged over 3 random splits

metrics.name: accuracy (FREE917)
metrics.definition: fraction of examples where predicted answer exactly matched the correct answer

metrics.name: accuracy (WEBQUESTIONS)
metrics.definition: F1 between predicted and annotated entity sets, giving partial credit

metrics.name: oracle score
metrics.definition: fraction of examples for which the beam contains any derivation with the correct denotation

baselines: Ablated system without bridging, denotation and alignment features on WEBQUESTIONS
eval.protocol: Held-out test sets (30% FREE917, 35% WEBQUESTIONS); ablations on development over 3 random splits; no significance test stated beyond the word 'significant'

availability.data: Both datasets released at the same URL

evidence.quote: We therefore allow partial credit and score an answer using the F1 measure, comparing the predicted set of entities to the annotated set of entities.

results.claim: On FREE917 the system trained on answers only beats Cai and Yates, who trained on logical forms.
results.setup: FREE917 test set (30% held out), entity lexicon of 1,100 manual entries given
results.quote: obtained 62% accuracy on the test set, outperforming the 59% accuracy reported by Cai and Yates (2013), who trained on full logical forms

results.claim: On WEBQUESTIONS the full system reaches 31.4% on the test set.
results.setup: WEBQUESTIONS test (35% held out), full system with lexicalized features, k=200
results.quote: whereas our full system obtains 31.4%, a significant improvement

results.claim: Baseline without bridging, denotation and alignment features scores 26.9% on the WEBQUESTIONS test set.
results.setup: Same setup, three main contributions removed
results.quote: The accuracy on the test set of this system is 26.9%

results.claim: Alignment alone gives 30.6% on WEBQUESTIONS dev; bridging alone 21.2%; combined 32.9%.
results.setup: Development set, avg of 3 random splits

results.claim: On FREE917 dev, bridging alone (66.9) beats alignment alone (38.0); combined 71.3.
Removing denotation features drops WEBQUESTIONS dev accuracy from 32.9 to 28.0 and FREE917 from 71.3 to 58.6.
Removing POS features drops WEBQUESTIONS dev accuracy to 28.9.
Lexicalized plus alignment features give the best WEBQUESTIONS dev accuracy, 36.4, but overfit on small FREE917.
100K Google Suggest questions were sent to AMT and 6,642 were annotated identically by at least two workers.
results.quote: Out of 100K questions, 6,642 were annotated identically by at least two AMT workers.
results.note: Table 3 lists 5,810 examples; the paper does not explain the gap between 6,642 and 5,810.

results.claim: WEBQUESTIONS has 5,810 examples and 4,525 word types.
Freebase used has 41M non-numeric entities, 19K properties, 596M assertions.
results.quote: which has 41M non-numeric entities, 19K properties, and 596M assertions

results.claim: Raising beam size gives tapering accuracy gains and a widening gap to oracle score.
results.setup: Fig 5, both datasets, k up to 500 (FREE917) and ~200 (WebQ)

limits: WEBQUESTIONS answers are restricted to the entity's Freebase page, so some gold answers are only roughly accurate (e.g. 'President of the United States' for James Madison) and partial answers occur.

WEBQUESTIONS accuracy (31.4%) is far below FREE917 (62%); authors attribute it to entity disambiguation over 41M entities, bridging failures when many binaries fit, and verbs drawn from subordinate clauses.
FREE917 uses a manual entity lexicon that simplifies entity disambiguation.
Questions are structurally simple (mostly one unary, one binary, one entity).
Learning rate, AdaGrad step size, regularisation and hardware not stated.
Gap between 6,642 agreed answers and 5,810 released examples is not explained.
